correctness.rationale: The mutually orthogonal spectral projectors f_gamma recover the tuple. The sum g of f_gamma d_gamma is 1 modulo J, satisfies f_gamma g = g d_gamma, and is invertible; conjugacy fixes the quotient pattern. The stabilizer is 1 plus the equal-color Peirce subspace W_c and orbit–stabilizer gives q^D. In fact the scheme check can be made over all test rings: on a fixed clopen coloring stratum, factor g=(1+x)b, where b is the color-block-diagonal part of g, invertible by nilpotence, and x has only off-color blocks in J. Uniqueness follows because two normalized conjugators differ on the right by an element of the block-diagonal stabilizer, and their block-diagonal parts are both 1. This is a polynomial chart with polynomial inverse, giving the claimed smooth, geometrically irreducible components of dimension D(c), in all characteristics. Conjugation preserves regular ranks, and for the canonical idempotents the regular images are direct sums of e_i A or A e_i. Expanding the edge factors gives the Fortuin–Kasteleyn formula. For fixed Peirce graph data across field orders, the infinitely many prime powers recover each q-polynomial; evaluation at q=1 recovers n and an arity allowing injective coloring recovers W by the exact degree. Substituting q=1/(1+v) and interpolating at the powers of two recovers Z, including W=0 or disconnected cases. This concerns a fixed dimension pattern, not canonical base change of an arbitrary algebra between characteristics. The path versus square-zero example changes J² without changing the ranks or Peirce data; reversing a fork interchanges the rank statistics, which are unequal already at arity one.
